\# Adds retention policy cancellation reason to Subscriptions

\## What’s new

Adds the \`canceled\_by\_retention\_policy\` enum value to the \[cancellation\_details.reason\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/object.md?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia#subscription\_object-cancellation\_details-reason) attribute on \[Subscription\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/object.md?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia) objects.

This value indicates that a subscription has been canceled automatically due to Stripe’s \[test data retention policy\](https://support.stripe.com/questions/test-mode-subscription-data-retention). This reduces confusion when reviewing test subscriptions that appear to have been canceled unexpectedly.

The retention policy only applies to subscriptions created in test mode or a sandbox. Therefore, the \`canceled\_by\_retention\_policy\` reason can only appear on subscriptions where \[livemode\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/object.md?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia#subscription\_object-livemode) is false.

\## Why is this a breaking change?

For subscriptions canceled by Stripe’s test data retention policy, the \`cancellation\_details.reason\` property is now \`canceled\_by\_retention\_policy\` instead of \`cancellation\_requested\`.

\## Impact

If your integration expects subscriptions canceled by the retention policy to have a \`cancellation\_details.reason\` of \`cancellation\_requested\`, then you need to update your code to expect a value of \`canceled\_by\_retention\_policy\` instead. Also, if your integration explicitly handles all possible values of \`cancellation\_details.reason\`, you need to update your code to handle the new \`canceled\_by\_retention\_policy\` value.

\| \`canceled\_by\_retention\_policy\` \| Added \| \[Subscription.cancellation\_details\](/api/subscriptions/object?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia#subscription\_object-cancellation\_details-reason) \|

\#### Ruby

This change doesn’t affect the Ruby SDK.

\#### Java

\#### .NET

This change doesn’t affect the .NET SDK.

\## Upgrade

\#### REST API

1\. \[View your current API version\](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.
2\. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the corresponding SDK version for this API version.
 \- If you don’t use an SDK, update your \[API requests\](https://docs.stripe.com/api-versions.md#how-versions-are-specified-in-requests) to include \`Stripe-Version: 2026-03-25.dahlia\`
3\. Upgrade the API version used for \[webhook endpoints\](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4\. \[Test your integration\](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5\. If you use Connect, \[test your Connect integration\](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).
